tur66-1: Surgery to remove the cyst is rare; if surgery is needed, it is usually the damage in the knee that is repaired, not the cyst itself.
tur66-2: It can; it is especially common for the cyst to go away on its own in children. In adults, because the cyst usually comes from another knee problem, symptoms often improve once that problem is treated. Recovery can take from a few months to a few years.
tur66-3: While running, jumping or making a sudden movement, did you feel a sharp pain in your calf, as if you had been stabbed? A calf strain happens when there is a small tear in one of the two large calf muscles. It is a common sports injury and usually settles within a few weeks. The right care in the first few days, followed by gradual exercise, supports recovery.
tur66-4: Sit with your leg straight and loop a towel or belt around the ball of your foot. Holding the ends, pull your foot towards you until you feel a gentle stretch in your calf.
tur66-5: Most people feel better in about 2 weeks, but to avoid another injury it is advised to avoid strenuous exercise for up to 8 weeks. Once you have full strength and full movement and can walk briskly without pain or swelling, start sport-specific movements and build up training gradually. In a study of 50 amateur athletes with a sudden tear in a thigh or calf muscle (about 40% of the injuries were in the calf), those who started loading exercises 2 days after the injury recovered pain-free and returned to sport a median of about 3 weeks sooner than those who started after 9 days; only one athlete had a re-injury, in the early-start group.

tur66-7: 10 days after the injury you still cannot put weight on your foot and your calf is still painful and swollen
tur66-8: Is your waist less than half your height? This simple ratio gives a practical estimate of whether fat is building up around your middle. NICE, the UK’s national health guidance body, advises adults with a body mass index under 35 to keep their waist to less than half their height. All you need is a tape measure: measure, then calculate below.
tur66-9: Yes. BMI shows excess weight but not where the fat is stored. Waist-to-height ratio is a practical estimate of fat around the middle. In a 2012 meta-analysis pooling studies, waist-to-height ratio was a better screening tool for heart and metabolic risk factors in adults than waist circumference or BMI. People from some ethnic backgrounds are more prone to storing fat around the middle, and their risk of weight-related conditions rises at a lower BMI. In a UK analysis using data from 1,453 adults, 35% of those judged to be at “no increased risk” by a chart based on BMI and waist circumference had a waist-to-height ratio of 0.5 or more.
